title: Unified Spectral, Dynamical, and Correlation Signatures of an Exceptional Point in Cavity Optomechanics
authors: Khazali Fahmi, Ahmad R. T. Nugraha, Ferry A. A. Nugraha, Adam B. Cahaya
abstract: We investigate how the exceptional-point structure of a dissipative cavity optomechanical system is inherited by experimentally accessible dynamical, spectral, and quantum-statistical observables. At optical-mechanical resonance, the effective non-Hermitian first-moment dynamics exhibits a second-order exceptional point, where two eigenvalues and their eigenvectors coalesce and the eigenvalue splitting follows the characteristic square-root dependence on perturbations. We show that the same square-root feature also governs transient photon and phonon populations, first-order coherence, spectral poles, and second-order intensity correlations. Below the exceptional point, the dynamics is non-oscillatory, whereas above it damped oscillations emerge together with frequency splitting of the spectral poles. At the exceptional point, the Jordan-block structure produces polynomial-exponential relaxation and a second-order spectral pole. Using the quantum regression theorem and Gaussian moment factorization, we further show that the stationary fluctuations satisfy the Siegert relation linking first- and second-order correlations. Although the zero-delay autocorrelations retain their thermal value, the finite-delay intensity correlations exhibit clear exceptional point signatures. This finding connects non-Hermitian mode coalescence with measurable dynamical and correlation observables in cavity optomechanics.
summary: This paper thoroughly examines the signatures of an exceptional point in a dissipative cavity optomechanical system. It demonstrates that the EP structure governs not only the system's eigenvalues but also the time evolution of photon/phonon populations and intensity correlations. The findings connect non-Hermitian mode coalescence directly to measurable quantum signatures in cavity optomechanics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the exceptional-point (EP) structure of a dissipative cavity optomechanical system manifests across various measurable quantum observables.
main_result: The EP causes a characteristic square-root dependence in eigenvalue splitting and dictates distinct dynamical regimes: non-oscillatory decay below the EP, polynomial-exponential decay at the EP, and damped oscillations above it.
method: The analysis combines theoretical modeling using the Lindblad master equation with the calculation of first- and second-order correlation functions and spectral responses.
model_or_system: The system is a dissipative cavity optomechanical setup involving an optical cavity coupled to a mechanical oscillator, modeled using an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Transient photon/phonon populations, first-order coherence, spectral poles, and second-order intensity correlations (g2).
important_parameters: The coupling strength ($g$) relative to the critical EP coupling ($g_{	ext{EP}}$), and the detunings ($\Delta, \omega_m$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the quantum regression theorem and Gaussian moment factorization to relate higher-order correlations to lower-order dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the eigenvalue splitting ($\Delta\lambda \propto \sqrt{\epsilon}$) across different coupling regimes and show the evolution of second-order correlation functions across the EP boundary.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system dynamics by first establishing the effective Hamiltonian, then examining the spectral signatures (eigenvalue splitting), and finally extending the analysis to time-domain observables like populations and correlations across the EP.
why_interesting: This work provides a comprehensive mapping of non-Hermitian physics (EPs) onto measurable, time-domain quantum observables (correlations, dynamics) in a highly relevant platform like cavity optomechanics.
